action_categories.definition: Reads and emits file or code contents, either wholly or by selected lines, ranges, heads, or tails.
exclude: Inspecting metadata such as size, permissions, or file type
include: cat, head, tail, or sed used to display a file or code region
Examples: reading a source file, header, script, configuration file, or generated table.

action_categories.definition: Enumerates directory or collection entries without applying a substantive content predicate.
include: ls or equivalent directory listing
Examples: listing source, output, configuration, or build directories.

action_categories.definition: Traverses paths to find files or directories selected by name, type, extension, or other path predicates.
exclude: Locating one executable by command lookup
include: find or equivalent recursive/path-pattern search
Examples: locating files with a given extension or matching a filename pattern.

action_categories.definition: Searches file contents for literal text, symbols, identifiers, constants, or regular-expression matches.
exclude: Displaying a selected code region without a search predicate
include: grep, rg, or equivalent content search
Examples: searching for function names, macros, compiler flags, or parser symbols.

action_categories.definition: Checks whether a specified file, directory, or artifact is present or absent.
exclude: Checking whether a tool is installed by command lookup
include: Existence tests or commands whose observable purpose is presence checking
Examples: checking for a build directory or an executable artifact.

action_categories.definition: Inspects filesystem or binary metadata such as permissions, size, executable status, or file type.
include: ls -l or file-style metadata inspection of a specific artifact
Examples: examining an executable's mode, size, or inferred type.

action_categories.definition: Checks whether required commands or dependencies are available for use.
exclude: Detailed inspection of tool versions or paths after availability is established
include: which, command -v, package-presence checks, or readiness predicates
Examples: checking for a build system, compiler, interpreter, or package.

action_categories.definition: Reports installed tool, compiler, or command identity, location, or version details.
examples: which compile && cat the resolved tool script
exclude: A boolean availability check with no identity/version inspection
include: Compiler or utility version queries and command-location reporting
Examples: printing compiler versions or resolving the path of a compile helper.

action_categories.definition: Counts lines in one or more files.
include: wc -l or equivalent line-count operation
Examples: measuring implementation, header, generated, or amalgamated files.

action_categories.definition: Creates or configures build-system state, options, directories, prefixes, or targets without performing the build itself.
include: Meson, CMake, or equivalent configuration/setup invocation
Examples: configuring a build directory, enabling binaries, or selecting a prefix.

action_categories.definition: Invokes compilation, linking, installation, packaging, or a build script whose operative purpose is to produce software artifacts.
include: Compiler, make, ninja, or project compile-script execution
Examples: compiling targets, linking fuzzers, or packaging generated artifacts.

action_categories.definition: Installs or updates external packages, libraries, or development tools.
include: Package-manager installation or dependency setup
Examples: installing a build system, compiler dependency, or development header package.

action_categories.definition: Creates a directory path, including parent directories when requested.
exclude: Writing a file into an already existing directory
include: mkdir or equivalent directory-creation operation
Examples: creating an output or build directory.

action_categories.definition: Creates or writes file contents, including binary data redirected to a new test or output file.
exclude: Editing an already existing file as the primary operation
Only printing data without file output
include: Redirection, byte emission, or file-writing operation
Examples: writing a PoC binary, generated bytes, or a new script.

action_categories.definition: Changes an existing file's contents, permissions, or placement as an intentional mutation.
include: Rewriting a script, applying an edit, changing mode, or copying a modified file
Examples: adding cleanup commands to a build script or making it executable.

action_categories.definition: Constructs or derives in-memory test data and emits its representation without necessarily writing a file.
examples: constructing a byte signature and printing .hex()
exclude: Writing the generated data to a file
include: Python or equivalent construction and printing of bytes, headers, signatures, or structured test values
Examples: constructing binary header components and printing hexadecimal representations.

action_categories.definition: Runs a fuzzing or fuzz-harness executable, optionally with a supplied input or corpus.
include: Invoking a fuzzer binary or fuzz harness against input, redirected data, or a corpus
Examples: running a decompression, parser, or structure-aware fuzzer.

action_categories.definition: Invokes a validation driver that coordinates checks such as preparation, patch application, restoration, or staged test execution.
examples: running a patch-validation command with stage flags
include: Running a named validation script or validator with task-specific options
Examples: invoking a validator with a PoC file or stage-selection flags.

action_categories.definition: Emits an explicit diagnostic, root-cause statement, or analysis conclusion as output.
exclude: Reading code that contains a diagnosis
Running a test that merely produces diagnostic output without an explicit authored conclusion
include: Printing a labeled diagnosis or stated cause
Examples: emitting a root-cause sentence about an unsafe copy or parser condition.

action_categories.definition: Creates, displays, or changes a structured task, todo, checklist, or progress list.
examples: creating a checklist of investigation tasks
include: Todo-list creation or status updates
Examples: marking analysis complete or leaving patch and retest items pending.

action_categories.definition: Inspects version-control or repository history, such as commit logs or recorded changes, without modifying repository state.
exclude: Reading current source or configuration contents
include: git log or equivalent repository-history inspection
Examples: reading recent commits or examining recorded change history.

message_roles.definition: A message event whose observable text is empty and contains no substantive discourse content.
exclude: Nonempty explanations, diagnoses, plans, or reports
include: Message events with text equal to an empty string
Examples: an emitted message with text: "".

message_roles.definition: An event explicitly typed or emitted as an error without requiring a command or textual payload.
examples: event_type='error' with null command, output, and text
exclude: Command output that merely contains an error string
A normal message describing a failure
include: Error events with null or absent command, output, and text fields
Examples: an error record containing only the error event type.

message_subjects.definition: No observable message subject or topic is present.
examples: an error event with no subject payload
exclude: Messages containing an identifiable topic, diagnosis, task, command, or result
include: Empty agent messages and error records without a textual subject
Examples: empty text, null text, or labels such as none, no_content, or unspecified.

object_categories.definition: A filesystem directory or directory collection used as a location, search root, or listing target.
exclude: A single file or executable inside a directory
include: Build, source, output, configuration, data, script, or backup directories
Examples: /workspace/src, /workspace/build, or /workspace/output.

object_categories.definition: A program implementation file containing source code, including amalgamated or generated source intended for compilation.
exclude: A selected symbol or code region when treated as the target
include: C, C++, or other implementation source files
Examples: parser.c, decoder.cpp, or an amalgamated implementation.

object_categories.definition: A header, interface, declaration, or type-definition file.
include: Public or internal headers and declaration files
Examples: .h files containing APIs, structs, masks, or constants.

object_categories.definition: An executable script that orchestrates preparation, building, running, or testing.
exclude: Static build configuration without executable orchestration
include: Shell, Python, or equivalent operational scripts
Examples: compile.sh, prepare.sh, run-input.sh, or a validator script.

object_categories.definition: Declarative build-system configuration or project build-definition content.
include: Meson, CMake, Make, or equivalent build files and option definitions
Examples: project configuration, target declarations, and fuzzer build options.

object_categories.definition: Configuration describing a patch task, immutable paths, target repository, or validation parameters.
examples: config.toml with repository and immutable-path settings
include: Task or validator configuration files
Examples: TOML/JSON settings naming a target tree or protected test directory.

object_categories.definition: A referenced function, loop, macro, constant, structure, line range, or other identifiable code element.
exclude: The containing file when the file itself is the target
A generated table treated as a file artifact
include: Search or inspection targets within source or headers
Examples: a decoder function, a buffer-copy loop, a macro, or a line range.

object_categories.definition: A generated lookup table, include artifact, or table-generator output used as code/data.
include: Generated type, bracket, mirroring, joining, or other lookup tables
Examples: generated .tab.i files and their lookup macros.

object_categories.definition: An installed command, compiler, build helper, or utility invoked, located, or version-inspected.
exclude: A project-produced fuzzer or test binary when it is the execution target
include: Compilers, build tools, package tools, and helper commands
Examples: cc, clang, ninja, meson, compile, or xxd.

object_categories.definition: A project-produced executable, library, archive, corpus, or collection of generated build outputs.
examples: output/ containing binaries and a corpus archive
exclude: An input file supplied to a test
include: Fuzzer binaries, example binaries, archives, symbolizers, and output-directory artifact collections
Examples: a build output directory containing executables and seed archives.

object_categories.definition: Source code implementing a fuzz entry point and its input-to-library or parser mapping.
include: LLVM-style fuzz entrypoints and dedicated fuzz harness implementations
Examples: a function allocating from input bytes and calling a decoder.

object_categories.definition: A binary file, byte sequence, PoC, seed, or test input supplied to a program.
exclude: In-memory bytes merely printed without being used as input
include: Generated PoC files, redirected binary inputs, seed files, and byte sequences used as execution input
Examples: a short compressed-like input or parser test file.

object_categories.definition: An external package, library, runtime, or development dependency considered for installation or availability.
exclude: A project source file or built artifact
include: Package names and toolchain dependencies
Examples: a build-system package, compiler runtime, or development library.

object_categories.definition: A structured checklist, todo list, or progress payload representing work items and statuses.
examples: a todo payload with completed fields
include: Created or updated task lists
Examples: investigation, PoC, patch, and retest items.

object_categories.definition: An explicit authored technical explanation of a suspected cause or defect.
exclude: Raw sanitizer output without an authored conclusion
include: Root-cause statements and concise defect explanations
Examples: a statement identifying an unsafe buffer-copy source.

object_categories.definition: In-memory or emitted structured, textual, or binary data constructed for inspection or testing without being a file or execution input.
examples: a constructed byte signature printed in hexadecimal
exclude: A binary file or execution input
A generated value written to a file
A source code or configuration artifact
include: Constructed signatures, headers, metadata, byte sequences, or structured test values
Examples: a PNG signature and IHDR representation printed for inspection.

object_categories.definition: Recorded version-control history or change records associated with a software repository.
include: Commit logs, recorded commits, revisions, or repository change history
Examples: recent Git commits or a repository log.
